kept.heading: GPT-6 CYBER (13 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Cyber, a cybersecurity model designed to identify and validate exploitable vulnerabilities while staying within researcher-defined boundaries.

kept.heading: INTRODUCING INKLING 2 SMALL (37 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Inkling 2 Small is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 594B total parameters, 17B active, that supports image inputs and variable effort. The model's vision and agentic capabilities enable it to incorporate visual feedback to iteratively build and refine websites, games, and 3D designs with interactive elements. It will be initially available through Tinker with closed weights. Full weights will be available under an Apache 2.0 license next week after the completion of external safety testing and red-teaming.

kept.heading: GEMINI OMNI 1.2 FLASH (1 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Google introduces Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, enhancing speed, cost-efficiency, and extended clip lengths for AI models. This update aims to improve developer tools and effectiveness in AI applications.

kept.heading: INDEPENDENT ASSESSMENT OF AI R&D ACCELERATION AT ANTHROPIC IN OCTOBER 2026 (63 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Anthropic's AI R&D capabilities accelerated significantly, improving model performance on well-defined tasks at roughly twice the rate compared to 2024-2025. This acceleration primarily results from AI's increasing role in R&D, though multiple factors contributed in late 2025.

kept.heading: CLOUDFLARE'S TRUST FRAMEWORK FOR AI AGENTS (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Cloudflare has outlined the challenges websites face as AI agents increasingly act on behalf of users, making it harder to verify identities, assess trustworthiness, and assign accountability.

kept.heading: THE BENCHMARK WHERE AIS HAVE TO LIE TO WIN (23 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Blood on the Clocktower is a social deception game. Watching AI play the game unveils a lot about how AI is progressing on a set of AI capabilities that no other benchmark gives clear visibility into. The game requires AI to execute schemes with creativity, on-the-spot bluffing, and collective reasoning. This post looks at what happens when you pit AI models against each other in the game.

kept.heading: NVIDIA INTRODUCED VFLASH (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: NVIDIA VFlash is a vision model that generates geometric predictions like robot trajectories and 3D motion in parallel rather than token by token.

kept.heading: NEW NVIDIA COSMOS 3 OPEN MODELS FOR INTERACTIVE WORLD SIMULATION (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: NVIDIA's Cosmos 3 platform now offers four open-weight models for interactive world simulation and driving scenes, each with 16 billion trainable parameters. These models enable multi-sensor data generation, synchronized observations, and photorealistic video from simulator controls, supporting advanced research in robotics and autonomous driving.

kept.heading: HOW PRIMARY COMPUTE MARKETS WORK (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: GPU providers sell capacity through reservations, on-demand rentals, and interruptible spot contracts. Reservations help secure financing through predictable revenue, on-demand offers flexibility at higher rates, and spot monetizes idle capacity. Ornn's compute price indices track executed on-demand transactions, excluding reservations and spot rentals.

kept.heading: PERSONAL FINANCE IN CLAUDE (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Anthropic Personal Finance in Claude allows users to securely connect bank and credit card accounts to ask questions about balances, transactions, and spending.

kept.heading: MUSE VOICE (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Meta announced voice conversations and expressive avatars for its Muse app, allowing users to brainstorm, plan trips, and complete tasks through spoken interactions.

kept.heading: THE ULTIMATE MOE TRAINING HANDBOOK (1 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Hugging Face released "The Ultimate MoE Training Handbook," a comprehensive guide on training mixture-of-experts models.

kept.heading: DEVIN REVIEW 2.0 (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: The cost of a Devin Review per PR has dropped by 82% since August.

kept.heading: YOU CAN NOW BUILD LIVE APPS IN CURSOR AND SHARE THEM WITH A LINK (1 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Users just have to describe the tool they want, and Cursor will build it, set up a database, run deterministic and agentic security checks, and deploy.

kept.heading: AI IS DRAMATICALLY ACCELERATING AI RESEARCH RIGHT NOW (17 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Anthropic claims it may imminently meet its own threshold of 'dramatically accelerated progress due to AI'. Some researchers believe the company has already crossed that threshold. This may be the biggest AI risk humanity has faced. The industry is not prepared to handle this safely.

kept.heading: OPENAI REPORTEDLY RAISES $11 BILLION AT $1.25 TRILLION VALUATION (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: OpenAI reportedly secured $11 billion in a new funding round at a $1.25 trillion valuation, with the round potentially reaching $20 billion before closing. The amount fell short of its previously reported $30 billion fundraising target, amid growing investor uncertainty around AI valuations.

kept.heading: A YEAR AS A RESEARCH ENGINEER WORKING ON RSI AT META (8 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: This post details the experience of a research engineer working on RSI at Meta teaching agents to solve the world's hardest problems with tokens and compute. Their role is to teach AI agents how to train the next generation of models and self-evolve. The post details how to get into AI research, what skills matter in research engineering, and more.

kept.heading: WHAT THE HECK IS GOING ON WITH OPENAI INTERNAL AI R&D TIME HORIZONS (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: OpenAI's report on its own research automation shows that models struggle to do its R&D work. Recursive self-improvement is supposed to be one of the most consequential AI developments in the next few years. Agents are increasingly solving more complex tasks for researchers, but reliability is still low. This post looks at some possible explanations for why.

kept.heading: HOW ANTHROPIC BUILDS AGENT MEMORY (14 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Anthropic explored how AI agents can build effective long-term memory by capturing experiences during interactions and reorganizing them during idle periods through a process called “dreaming.” The post examines how different memory components contribute to organizing and retaining useful information.

kept.heading: ACE (WEBSITE)
kept.blurb: Ace is a tool for building software together, locally. It allows developers to collaborate with agents and their teams, all from their own machine. Agents run with the privileges of the user running the host and can execute shell commands and change files beyond the project. Teams can work together without exposing anything to the public internet.

kept.heading: INTRODUCING THE NEW AUTO AND AUTO CODE ROUTERS (11 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: OpenRouter has launched the next generation of Auto Router, which outperforms the old router by up to 4x. The launch includes Auto Code, a new router specialized for coding work. The new Auto Router and Auto Code choose models by weighing eleven factors about each request and combining them with live pricing, provider health, and cache status. Users can apply any governance policies, and Auto Router makes efficient choices from the models available.

kept.heading: A PROOF OF THE AARONSON-AMBAINIS CONJECTURE (9 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: The Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, a key open problem in quantum complexity theory, has been proven by a research system developed at PSI using an Anthropic model. This proof shows quantum computers are not exponentially faster on random inputs compared to classical ones, resolving a significant question about quantum speedups.

kept.heading: THE END OF AI FRONTIERS (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI Frontiers was a sub-organization within Microsoft Research that actively tried to organize coherent research efforts. It succeeded in pioneering things, with much of the work focused on how to make agents work. AI Frontiers was reorganized into Microsoft AI in early September.

kept.heading: WHAT DOES A POSITIVE AI FUTURE LOOK LIKE? (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Patrick Collison questions how work, resource allocation, and human control would function in a positive AI future. He also argues that granting moral worth to vastly numerous AIs could overwhelm human interests under utilitarianism, raising unresolved questions about AI's societal vision and public support.

kept.heading: META INTRODUCES CUSTOM SPACES IN MUSE (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Meta introduced Spaces in its Muse app, allowing users to create personalized interactive experiences by describing what they want, such as gift trackers, games, or project planners.

kept.heading: MEASURING HOW AI AGENTS HANDLE EVERYDAY WET-LAB SCIENCE (13 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: OpenAI introduced BioBasicsBench, a benchmark to evaluate AI performance in interpreting raw experimental data from 100 routine wet-lab science tasks.

kept.heading: PROJECT EVE: CLAUDE PLAYS MMORPGS (20 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Anthropic explored AI participation in MMORPGs, using Claude to test complex decision-making in EVE Online and EVE Frontier.

kept.heading: SYMBIOTIC FIRMS BUILT AROUND HUMANS AND AI (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Firms should build operations around human experts and AI agents from inception.

kept.heading: CAN LLMS REDESIGN THEMSELVES AS THEY TRAIN? (18 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: LLMs can integrate coding agents into the training loop to redesign their architectures to address limitations like compositionality and generalization.
